description: Registry of ADCOS core domain objects (the frozen architecture nouns of spec/architecture.md §6). Each entry maps a frozen noun to a stable, technology-neutral identifier and its versioned machine-readable schema definition. Core object identifiers never encode an access technology, radio generation, vendor, or implementation language (architecture §2 P1/P2, §25). Access technologies are data in the access-profile registry, never core domain types (LOCK-001..LOCK-003).

adcos.adapter.description: Typed implementation boundary around a physical or logical access technology (architecture §6.3).

adcos.capability.description: Signed, versioned statement describing something the node or adapter may provide (architecture §6.4).

adcos.evidence.description: Cryptographically attributable observation supporting a claim, with explicit provenance (architecture §6.11, LOCK-008).

adcos.federation.description: Typed relationship between administrative domains allowing selected capabilities and services to be shared (architecture §6.10, §21).

adcos.identity.description: Asymmetric-key-backed node identity, independent of access technology (architecture §6.2, LOCK-005).

adcos.intent.description: Machine-readable request describing desired connectivity properties rather than the technology used to obtain them (architecture §6.9, LOCK-019).

adcos.link.description: Directional or bidirectional connectivity relationship between two adapters; link state is independent of node identity and advertisement freshness (architecture §6.5, §11).

adcos.node.description: Cryptographically identified participant in the ADCOS fabric (architecture §6.1, §4).

adcos.path.description: Ordered set of links that can satisfy a session or resource intent (architecture §6.6).

adcos.resource.description: Consumable or reservable quantity such as throughput, compute, storage, energy, or service capacity (architecture §6.8, §17).

adcos.session.description: Logical connectivity relationship independent of a particular radio bearer; session identity is access-independent (architecture §6.7, LOCK-006).
